name: AI21 Labs
h1: AI21 Labs ARR: ~$350M in Enterprise LLMs.
intro: AI21 Labs — the Tel Aviv lab founded in 2019, older than most of this leaderboard — reached a ~$350M estimated annualized run rate in 2026 by selling efficient enterprise LLMs: the Jamba model family, the Maestro orchestration platform and the Wordtune writing product. Every reported figure is collected below, each traced back to a public source; AI21 has not officially disclosed revenue.

modelTitle: How Cheap Jamba Tokens Win Enterprise Workloads.
modelParagraphs: AI21's model is enterprise efficiency: the Jamba family (hybrid SSM-Transformer architecture) is sold on a usage-based API with per-token pricing positioned well below frontier-lab rates, optimized for long-context, high-throughput workloads where cost per million tokens is the buying criterion. Jamba models are also offered open-weight for private deployment, mirroring the sovereign/enterprise playbook.

Two adjacent products round out the mix: Maestro, an agentic orchestration platform that composes AI21 and third-party models into enterprise workflows (the strategic focus of the 2025 Google/Nvidia-backed round), and Wordtune, the consumer writing assistant that was AI21's first product and still contributes a consumer revenue base.

faqs.q: What Is AI21 Labs' ARR in 2026?
faqs.a: Third-party estimates put AI21 Labs at roughly $350 million in annualized revenue for 2026, up from an estimated ~$50M in 2025. AI21 itself has never officially disclosed revenue, so this figure should be treated as an estimate.

faqs.q: How Does AI21 Labs Make Money?
faqs.a: Three ways: usage-based API pricing on the Jamba model family (efficient hybrid SSM-Transformer LLMs sold well below frontier-lab rates), the Maestro agentic orchestration platform for enterprises, and Wordtune consumer subscriptions.

faqs.q: What Is AI21 Labs' Valuation and How Much Has It Raised?
faqs.a: About $1.5 billion, following a $300 million Series D in May 2025 backed by Google and Nvidia. Total raised across seven rounds is roughly $636 million, after a ~$208M Series C at ~$1.4B in November 2023.

Jamba is the first production-grade hybrid of Mamba-style state-space models and Transformers, giving it a much larger effective context window at far lower memory and cost per token — the efficiency argument that wins cost-sensitive enterprise buyers.

faqs.q: How Does AI21 Compare to Other AI Labs by Revenue?
faqs.a: Its ~$350M estimated ARR puts it in the same band as Mistral ($400M, Jan 2026) and Cohere (~$500M est.) but far behind OpenAI (~$25B) and Anthropic ($65B+) — a reminder that the enterprise-efficiency segment of the LLM market is an order of magnitude smaller than the frontier-consumer segment.
